questions.question: Among the following, whose autobiography is ‘Daughter of Destiny: An Autobiography’?

The correct answer is Benazir Bhutto.

Additional Information

  • Malala Yousafzai is a Pakistani activist for female education and the 2014 Nobel Peace Prize laureate. Awarded when she was 17, she is the world's youngest Nobel Prize laureate, and the second Pakistani and the first Pashtun to ever receive a Nobel Prize.

questions.question: Surendranath Banerjee's autobiography is called ____________
questions.questionHtml: Surendranath Banerjee's autobiography is called ____________
questions.solution:
The correct answer is A Nation in the Making.

Key Points

  • Sir Surendranath Banerjee often known as Rashtraguru was an Indian nationalist leader during British Rule.
  • He founded a nationalist organization called the Indian National Association and was one of the founding members of the Indian National Congress.
  • Surendranath supported Montagu–Chelmsford Reforms, unlike Congress, and with many liberal leaders he left Congress and founded a new organization named Indian National Liberation Federation in 1919.
  • Surendranath Banerjee was born in Calcutta, in the province of Bengal to a Rarhi Kulin Brahmin family, suggesting that the ancestral seat of the family was in the Rarh region of present-day West Bengal.
  • In 1879, he bought the newspaper, The Bengalee(founded in 1862 by Girish Chandra Ghosh) and edited it for 40 years in b, when Banerjee was arrested for publishing remarks in his paper.

Additional Information

  • A Nation in the Making written in the last years of Sir Surendranath Banerjea's life, is not only the autobiography of a pioneering leader in Indian politics but also a commentary on public life.
  • This book is originally published in 1925.

questions.question: ‘Vikramarjuna - Vijaya’ composed by Pampa was written in which of the following languages?
questions.questionHtml: ‘Vikramarjuna - Vijaya’ composed by Pampa was written in which of the following languages?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Kannada.

Key Points

  • The annals of Kannada literature are incomplete without the mention of Adikavi Pampa, a revered poet of the 10th century.
  • Known as the first poet of the language, Pampa's works were primarily in Kannada, and he was a firm believer in Jainism.
  • His two epic works, Vikramarjuna Vijaya or Pampa Bharata and the Adi Purana, written around 939 CE, were composed in the champu style and served as court poems for the Vemulavada Chalukyan king Arikesari II.
  • Pampa also held a position as a feudatory under the Rashtrakuta dynasty king Krishna III.
  • His works set the foundation for all subsequent Kannada champu compositions and marked a significant beginning for the 10th century in Kannada literature, alongside the works of two other Jain authors, Sri Ponna and Ranna, collectively known as the “Three gems of Kannada literature”.

Additional Information

  • Kannada first female poet
    • Akka Mahadevi (circa 1130 – 1160) emerged as a significant figure in 12th-century Kannada literature and played a prominent role within the Lingayat Shaiva sect.
    • She is renowned as one of the pioneering female poets of this era.
  • Adikavi (adi ‘primaeval, first’ + kavi ‘poet’) means ‘the first poet’.
